barRaise.topFinding: One thing in the product itself is actually broken, and it is in the export path rather than the print path everyone assumed was the risk. PNG export rasterizes the print stage through html2canvas outside print media, so the gap and stacking rules that live only inside the print block never apply, and a back-enabled label at large or xl comes out laid in a fixed-width row that both diverges from the browser's own print output and overflows the 8.5 inch box (src/util/export-png.js:48-58 against styles/label.css:460-478 and the class stamped at src/render.js:582). Everything the last review flagged as shipping wrong content is genuinely fixed and was re-measured rather than read off the changelog: zero em dashes remain anywhere in the data, the source or the docs, the contrast gate really does target 4.5 and really does run pre-commit, and the blind git-lock delete is gone from the status writer. The count of open actions jumps from 8 to 34 because this was a full 30-lens fan-out against a project that had not had one in a week, and because 16 of the 34 are the shared orchestration layer rather than this repository: the stale plugin snapshot, the skill-routing clauses that sit in body prose where the router never reads them, and this very orchestrator's steps 7 and 8 pointing a session at the generated public status file instead of the canonical one. The thing worth Kane's attention above all of it is not a bug: ten weeks after the v1.0 cut, every commit here has been review-machinery output and no roadmap item has moved, which is the same profile that earned Cattery and Scheduler an explicit dead-for-now ruling.
